article.story:
Florian Wirtz scored a brace -- including a stellar individual goal for his first -- as Germany finished top of Group A2 in the Nations League with a stunning 5-0 victory over the Netherlands in Berlin on Monday.

The hosts opened the scoring just before the break through Derry Scherhant's impressive top-corner finish, which was the winger's first international goal. Scherhant, who used to score such goals in the same stadium for Hertha Berlin, pointed to the ground to indicate he was home again.

"You couldn't have imagined it going any better," said Scherhant, who now plays for Freiburg.

Germany quickly took control in the second half with three goals in the space of 11 minutes thanks to Wirtz's double and a Nico Schlotterbeck effort.

Brajan Gruda, who had already provided two assists, then got on the scoresheet to secure Germany's spot at the top on 11 points in extraordinary circumstances.

With Greece beating Serbia, Jürgen Klopp's side needed to beat the Dutch by at least a five-goal margin and they managed to do just that to sit at the summit, with the Netherlands sitting in second on goal difference to book their place in the Nations League quarterfinals. Greece, also on 11 points, finished third.

Schlotterbeck sealed the result five minutes later with a low header to Gruda's free kick, and Wirtz volleyed in his second in the 71st after Gruda was left free on the right. It prompted some Dutch fans to head for the exits.

Gruda got Germany's fifth in the 77th, prompting furious Dutch goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen to call a team meeting to remonstrate with his teammates. By then it was too late.

Klopp made two changes to the team who beat Serbia 3-1 on Friday as Nico Schlotterbeck and Nathaniel Brown lined up in defence and Quinten Timber was the sole change in the Netherlands starting lineup after they thumped Greece 7-0.

The game marked the last time that Germany would sport their signature Adidas kit for at least the next 10 years after the country's federation agreed to a sponsorship deal with Nike.

Adidas had been the the equipment and jersey sponsor for Germany since the 1954 World Cup.

Information from PA and The Associated Press was used in this recap.
